subject.title: fix: guarded fetch falls back to IPv6 when IPv4 is unreachable

question: Should guarded SSRF fetches pass every already-validated address family to Node family auto-selection, replacing the current IPv4-only result for `{ all: true }` lookups?
rationale: This is a deliberate availability and SSRF-connection-policy tradeoff: the current IPv4 preference was introduced after an IPv6-unreachable failure, while the PR restores IPv6 candidates to solve the converse route failure.

options.title: Adopt dual-family fallback after proof
options.body: Accept the proposed all-record behavior after the contributor supplies redacted same-head guarded-fetch evidence for both asymmetric-route directions and an owner confirms the policy.

options.title: Retain IPv4-only behavior
options.body: Keep the current mitigation and pursue a different owner-approved fallback design if IPv6-only provider connectivity must be supported.

recommendation.title: Adopt dual-family fallback after proof
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed all-record behavior after the contributor supplies redacted same-head guarded-fetch evidence for both asymmetric-route directions and an owner confirms the policy.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the current IPv4-preference behavior that the PR selectively relaxes.
